stages.name: Unmanaged
stages.short_description: No Conditional Access in use. Identity is protected, if at all, by Security Defaults or nothing.
stages.typical_tenant: Brand-new Microsoft 365/Entra tenant, or a tenant that's never had a dedicated identity/security owner. Usually SMB or a proof-of-concept environment that grew organically.
characteristics: Either Security Defaults is on (all-or-nothing MFA for all users) or fully off
No custom Conditional Access policies exist
No break-glass/emergency access accounts
Legacy authentication protocols (POP, IMAP, SMTP AUTH, older Office clients) still allowed
No visibility into sign-in risk or device compliance
risks_of_staying_here: Security Defaults is rigid — can't exclude break-glass accounts, can't tune for specific apps, breaks legitimate legacy-auth workflows without warning
No protection against password-spray/credential-stuffing beyond baseline MFA
No way to differentiate risk for admins vs. regular users
stages.graduation_trigger: As soon as there's a dedicated IT/security owner and more than a handful of users, move to Stage 1 — Security Defaults does not scale and cannot be selectively tuned.

stages.name: Foundational
stages.short_description: Security Defaults replaced with a small set of custom baseline policies covering the highest-value risks.
stages.typical_tenant: Organization with a named IT/security lead, under ~500 users, first real investment in identity security.
characteristics: Security Defaults turned OFF, replaced by custom policies
Break-glass emergency access accounts created, excluded from all CA policies, monitored separately
MFA required for all users (not just admins)
MFA required for all admin roles specifically, ideally with a tighter/stronger control than standard users
Legacy authentication blocked tenant-wide
Basic naming convention and documentation for policies established
risks_of_staying_here: Still largely binary (allow/block) — no risk signal, no device posture check
No differentiation between a login from a managed corporate laptop and an unknown device
No handling of guest/external user access separate from employees
stages.graduation_trigger: Once baseline MFA + legacy-auth blocking is stable (no help-desk fire drills, break-glass tested), move to Stage 2 by introducing device- and app-specific controls.
stages.estimated_effort_to_next_stage: 2-6 weeks, mostly change-management and communication, not technical build

stages.name: Standard
stages.short_description: Policies differentiate by application sensitivity and device compliance, not just identity.
stages.typical_tenant: Mid-size organization, Intune or another MDM in place, starting to care about data sensitivity per app.
characteristics: Device compliance policies (Intune) exist and are referenced in CA — e.g. require compliant or hybrid-joined device for sensitive apps
Session controls introduced — sign-in frequency, persistent browser session restrictions for unmanaged devices
Separate, stricter policies for high-value apps (finance systems, HR, admin portals) vs. general SaaS
Guest/external user access explicitly scoped and restricted (not inheriting employee policies by default)
Location-based conditions in use (e.g. block or step-up MFA for atypical countries) as a coarse control
Report-only mode used before enforcing new policies
Named locations configured (trusted/corporate IP ranges) rather than relying on country alone
risks_of_staying_here: Still largely static rules — a compromised credential with a compliant device and normal location still gets in
No real-time risk scoring; a leaked password looks the same as a legitimate login if other signals match
Policies often accumulate without a review cadence, leading to overlap or conflict
stages.graduation_trigger: Once device compliance and app-tiering are stable and report-only testing is a routine part of the change process, move to Stage 3 by adding Identity Protection risk signals.
stages.estimated_effort_to_next_stage: 1-3 months, needs Entra ID P2 licensing for Identity Protection

stages.name: Advanced
stages.short_description: Risk-based, adaptive policies using Identity Protection sign-in and user risk signals.
stages.typical_tenant: Larger organization or one in a regulated industry, has Entra ID P2, dedicated identity/security team.
characteristics: Identity Protection enabled — user risk and sign-in risk feed directly into CA policies
Risk-based policies: e.g. medium sign-in risk triggers MFA step-up, high user risk forces password reset or blocks access
Authentication strengths configured — phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2/passkeys, certificate-based auth) required for high-sensitivity access, not just 'any MFA'
Privileged Identity Management (PIM) integrated with CA — just-in-time admin role activation requires its own CA-enforced step-up
Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) enabled for supported apps — near-real-time token revocation on risk/location change, not just at sign-in
Terms of Use and Insider Risk signals incorporated where relevant
Regular access reviews tied to policy exclusions and admin role assignments
Formal policy governance: change process, testing in report-only, rollback plan, periodic audit of exclusions
risks_of_staying_here: Coverage may still be inconsistent across all app types, especially legacy/on-prem-integrated apps
Cross-tenant and B2B/B2C scenarios often lag behind the core employee policy set
Network-layer control (what happens after token issuance, for unmanaged internet-bound traffic) usually still a gap
stages.graduation_trigger: Once risk-based policies and phishing-resistant auth are the default for privileged access, and CAE is broadly deployed, move to Stage 4 by extending control to network/session layer and cross-tenant scenarios.
stages.estimated_effort_to_next_stage: 3-6+ months, organizational maturity as much as technical

stages.name: Optimized / Zero Trust
stages.short_description: Conditional Access is one layer of a fully integrated Zero Trust control plane spanning identity, device, network, and app layers.
stages.typical_tenant: Enterprise with mature security program, often regulated (finance, energy, government-adjacent), dedicated Zero Trust initiative.
characteristics: Global Secure Access (Entra Internet Access / Private Access) integrated — CA policies extend to network-layer traffic, not just app sign-in
Phishing-resistant authentication is the default baseline for all users, not just privileged ones
Continuous Access Evaluation extended across the full app estate, including custom/line-of-business apps where feasible
Cross-tenant access settings and B2B collaboration governed with the same rigor as internal CA policy
Automated policy testing/CI for CA changes — 'policy as code' via Graph API/Terraform, changes reviewed like software changes
Continuous monitoring and automated response — Sentinel/XDR signals feed back into risk policies, not just Identity Protection's own signals
Regular red-team/attack-simulation validation of CA coverage (e.g. testing token theft, session hijack scenarios against CAE)
Formal maturity review cadence — policies re-assessed against new threats and new Entra features on a fixed schedule
risks_of_staying_here: This stage requires ongoing investment to maintain — Zero Trust degrades quietly if governance lapses
Feature/licensing changes from Microsoft can shift what 'optimized' looks like; this stage needs a maintenance owner, not just a one-time project
stages.graduation_trigger: N/A — this is a maintenance stage. Re-assess quarterly against new Entra/Zero Trust capabilities.
